# Proposal 3: devices as data, code generated from research (2026-10-30)

Angle: maximum speed for each new projector. A projector is a data folder. The HAL code tables, the HAL allow
lists, the feature table, the stock behaviour knobs and the settings menus are generated from that folder by
tools. Hand-written Java is either shared (one copy, in a core) or device-only (a small plugin). Nobody copies a
file to change one condition any more.

Inputs: `MAP_apps.md`, `MAP_image.md`, `MAP_checks.md` in this folder, plus the files cited below. All paths are
relative to `gsi/`. Nothing outside this file was changed while writing it.

## 1. Short answer

- The stock XGIMI software already works this way, and we can copy it. The HB stock settings APK carries a node
  catalogue (`res/raw/picture.json`, 244 nodes with `nodeId`, `type`, `text`, `map`, `action`) and **98 product
  trees** (`res/raw/settings_tree_product_<name>.json`), one per XGIMI projector, plus the per-unit switch file
  `/mnt/vendor/xgimiconfig/<model>/feature/feature.xml` (read by `HbFeatures.java`). The Z9X is `dapeng`
  (`research/z9x_stock_settings/settings_tree_product_dapeng.json`), the HB is `dapengse`. A future XGIMI
  projector on the same software family very likely already has its tree in that list.
- We already generate the hardest part for one device: `devices/goat_elegant/research/gen/regen.sh` turns the
  stock vendor libraries into `aidl_codes.tsv`, `name_map.tsv` and `banned.tsv`. Today those tables are only
  read by a checker; the Java that sends the codes is still written by hand (`AidlCaller.java`, 715 lines) and
  must agree with the table. This proposal turns the direction around: the table is the source, the Java is
  generated, and the allow list is the same table, so they cannot disagree.
- Proposed shape: one `core/` (shared Java, UI engine, HAL transports), one `tools/gen/` (generators), and per
  device `devices/<codename>/` (data plus a small optional plugin). One command, `lumen`, runs survey, gen, build,
  check, image and prove for any device from the registry.
- A new projector of a known family (MediaTek, HIDL or AIDL gmpf) drops from about 3 to 4 weeks of copying and
  hand forks to about 5 to 8 working days, most of it device testing against stock (section 5).
- Z9X: during stages 0 to 6 nothing the Z9X gate reads is edited, so the Z9X stays byte-identical and the
  existing gate and proof bundle keep proving it. The Z9X moves onto the core only at a planned Z9X release
  (stage 7). At that point its APKs change bytes. The owner must accept that byte identity is replaced by a
  behavioural proof for that one release (section 6).

Rules of the shape:

1. Core code never branches on device identity. It asks a question of generated data: `Features.has(F.ULTRA_120)`,
   `DeviceBehaviour.KEYSTONE_RESET`, `MenuSpec.page("picture")`. `Device.isPlay6()` style checks are not allowed
   in core (a check in `lumen check` greps for them).
2. A HAL op that a device does not map is generated as "unsupported". Its menu nodes and tiles are dropped at
   generation time, so a disabled row cannot exist (owner rule: hide unsupported).
3. Generated code is plain Java constants and arrays. No JSON parsing, no reflection at runtime. Weak hardware
   pays nothing for the data-driven design (owner rule: fast on weak).
4. A device may override a core component only through a `DevicePlugin` seam. A whole-file override
   (`devices/X/overrides/<path>`) exists as an escape hatch, is listed by `lumen check`, and shows a count; the
   target is zero.

## 3. What goes where

### 3.1 HAL: research tables to generated code

Today:
- Z9X: codes are Java constants in `apps/Z9xProjector/src/org/lumen/projector/hal/GmpfClient.java` (1,560 lines,
  for example `SET_AUDIO_OUTPUT = 59` at line 61) and `Gmpf2Client.java`; the banned list is a Python dict in
  `apps/check_hal_callers.py:29`.
- Play 6: `research/play6/gmpf_codes_play6.tsv` (937 rows), renamed clients `Play6Gmpf`, `Play6Gmpf2`.
- HB: `devices/goat_elegant/research/{aidl_codes,allowed,banned,name_map}.tsv`, hand-written `AidlCaller.java`
  plus hand-written `GmpfClient`, `Gmpf2Client` with Z9X names.

Target:
- `core/hal/ops.tsv`: the Lumen op catalogue, one row per semantic operation the core uses
  (`setAudioOutput(u8)->void`, `getKeystonePoints()->KstPoint[]`, ...). About 150 rows: HB already sends 143
  calls and the Z9X checker counts 152 caller sites (`MAP_checks.md` section 5).
- `devices/X/hal/codes.tsv`: everything the vendor offers (generated by survey: `ndk_codes.py`, `java_codes.py`
  for AIDL; `hidl_hash.py`, `gmpf_layout.py` for HIDL, all of which exist today).
- `devices/X/hal/map.tsv`: op, service, code, codec, note. First filled automatically by matching names (today's
  `name_map.py`), then reviewed. This table is the allow list.
- `tools/gen/halgen.py` emits `HalCodes.java` and the `GmpfClient` / `Gmpf2Client` facades with the Z9X class
  names and signatures (the HB proved that keeping the names lets 90 percent of files stay shared), each method a
  call through `core/hal` `Transport` with a named codec. Templates per transport: `hidl.tmpl`, `aidl.tmpl`.
- `halgen.py` refuses to emit a code that is BANNED in `banned.tsv`, and stops on a REVIEW row unless the map row
  carries an owner note. The ban is enforced before compile, not only after.
- The checker becomes one table-driven tool (the model is `tools/devices/check_aidl_hal.py`): every transact in the
  dex is a map row and every map row is a transact. The fixed count in `check_aidl_hal_test.sh` (141, now 143) is
  replaced by "equal to the number of map rows".

### 3.2 Features and behaviour knobs

- `devices/X/features.tsv` replaces `HbFeatures.java` (30 features, ON/OFF/PENDING), the Z9X constants such as
  `Z9xFitDevice.SUPPORTED`, and Play 6 identity checks. Columns: feature, state, feature.xml key, off values,
  proof. `featgen.py` emits `Features.java` with the same runtime feature.xml cross-check `HbFeatures.init()`
  does today. Survey pre-fills it from feature.xml and the stock product tree.
- `devices/X/behaviour.conf` holds the stock differences that today cost a whole-file fork. From `MAP_apps.md`
  section 7: keystone reset path (HB 38/84/85), zoom dial limits, eye-guard gear key, wake-by-OK focus hold, lamp
  dim with dynamic black, timer lamp, SPDIF off, sound EQ preset set, fit device id. The 7 HB forks of 30 lines or
  fewer (`FitDevices`, `TimerLamp`, `EyeGuard`, `SoundEq`, `DreamLamp`, `SpdifOff`, `SetupBridgeProvider`) become
  one line each. Unknown keys are an error, so a typo cannot silently fall back to Z9X behaviour.

### 3.3 Menus from a declarative spec

- `core/menu/catalog.json`: Lumen node catalogue, modelled on stock `picture.json`: `nodeId`, kind (toggle,
  choice, slider, nav, action, panel), string id, `map` of values, the HAL op pair (getter, setter) or a Java
  action name, required feature, tips. One catalogue for all devices.
- `devices/X/menu/tree.json`: the page tree, same shape as stock `settings_tree_product_*.json`
  (`{"nodeId":"root","page":[...]}`). `tools/gen/menu_import.py` converts the stock tree of that product into a
  Lumen tree through `core/menu/stock_ids.tsv` (stock nodeId to Lumen nodeId). Stock nodes with no Lumen node are
  printed as a to-do list, which is the parity survey done by a tool instead of by hand.
- `menugen.py` resolves the tree against the catalogue, the device map and the features, drops every node whose
  op is unmapped or whose feature is not ON, and emits `MenuSpec.java` (static arrays). `core/ui` MenuEngine
  builds pages with the existing row classes (`SliderRow`, `ToggleRow`, `ChoiceRow`, `NavRow`, `PagedPanel`).
- Complex screens stay code: manual keystone (1,378 lines), optical zoom, fit, AK overlay. The tree references
  them as `panel` nodes by class name; a device-only panel lives in its plugin.
- Stock order and grouping come from the stock tree, so "stock 1:1 first" becomes the default instead of a
  per-page manual comparison.

### 3.4 Strings

One generator (extend `apps/i18n/gen.py` logic into `core/i18n`, absorb `tools/play6/gen_play6_i18n.py`). Source
format `langs/*.txt` for core and for each device. `lumen check` fails when a string used by the generated menu
lacks any of the 17 locales. This would have caught `strings_hb_fit.xml` missing ar, be, kk, pt-rBR, tr, uk.

### 3.5 Image, signing, installer, publishing

- One composer `tools/image/compose.py` with a step library (debloat, pinned apps, privapp files, props, rc, audio,
  file system). `image.conf` is the only list; the duplicated stage list inside `compose_hb.sh` and the 38-path
  array in `tools/play6/compose.sh` go away. The composer first prints a plan (ordered operations); the plan is
  what checks compare.
- One signer reading `devices/X/image/sign.conf` (the pinned list today exists twice: `sign_play6.py:134` and
  `sign.conf:12`). Keys in one layout `~/.lumen-keys/<codename>`.
- Installer: flows as scripts in `installer/flows/<install_flow>.sh` (and `.ps1`), chosen by the registry key.
  `installer/lib/devices.conf` is generated from the registry. The ab-fastbootd flow (designed, "Step 7 ... NOT
  done", `devices/IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md:108`) is built once and then serves every A/B virtual device.
- Publish rules come from `devices/X/publish.rules` plus registry defaults, so a fourth device does not produce
  REVIEW rows that stop the export (`MAP_checks.md` 6.3).

## 4. The `lumen` command

| Command | Does | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `lumen survey X` | pull props, vendor libs, settings APK over adb or from a dump; run extractors; write `hal/codes.tsv`, draft `map.tsv`, draft `features.tsv`, draft `menu/tree.json`, to-do report | 1 to 3 h, mostly copying |
| `lumen new-device X --like Y` | create `devices/X/` from a template, fill `device.conf` from survey | minutes |
| `lumen gen X` | all generators into `build/gen/X/` | seconds |
| `lumen build X` | gen, compile core + plugin, host tests with X's data, sign with X's key | 1 to 2 min |
| `lumen check X` | registry, gen up to date, HAL, menu, strings, overrides count, plugin API, publish rules, Z9X gate | 1 to 5 min |
| `lumen image X tN` | compose plan, compose, sign, verify | builder time |
| `lumen prove z9x` | today's `prove_unchanged.sh`, with exit codes and hashes instead of counts in text | about 5 min |
| `lumen record z9x --reason "..."` | the one re-record command, keeps the dated copy, writes the reason | 5 min |

`lumen check all` runs every device, the HB included (today the HB is in no combined run).

## 5. Adding a new projector

Step list, for a projector of a known family (MediaTek, gmpf over HIDL or AIDL, A/B or single slot that already
has a flow). Times are working time, rough, based on the HB round.

| # | Step | Who | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stock dump: partitions, props, vendor libs, settings APK, feature.xml (existing fastbootd and dump routines) | dev + owner device | 0.5 day |
| 2 | `lumen survey X`, then `lumen new-device X --like goat_elegant` | tool | 1 to 3 h |
| 3 | Review `hal/map.tsv`: confirm auto-matched ops, write codecs for new structs, set banned verdicts | dev | 1 to 2 days |
| 4 | Review `features.tsv` (pre-filled from feature.xml and stock tree), mark PENDING what is unproven | dev | 0.5 day |
| 5 | Review `menu/tree.json` and the to-do list of unmapped stock nodes | dev | 0.5 day |
| 6 | `gen_device_keys.sh X` | owner | 15 min |
| 7 | `image.conf`, props, rc and audio files under `devices/X/image/` | dev | 1 day |
| 8 | `lumen build X`, `lumen check X`, `lumen image X t1` | tool | builder time |
| 9 | First boot and fix loop (platform specific, cannot be generated) | dev + owner device | 1 to 3 days |
| 10 | Behaviour knobs: test each stock behaviour over adb, set `behaviour.conf`, PENDING features to ON | dev | 1 to 2 days |
| 11 | Device-only features as a plugin, only if the device has hardware the others lack | dev | 0 to n days |
| 12 | `lumen check all`, `lumen prove z9x` | tool | 10 min |

Total to a first test image with the full menu: about 5 to 8 working days. The large manual parts of today (a
550-line composer fork, a few hundred forked app files, a hand-written HAL caller, hand-written strings) are gone.

Slower cases:
- A new HAL transport or a different SoC (not gmpf): new transport template and codecs, add 1 to 2 weeks once.
- A new install flow: one flow script in sh and ps1, add about 1 week once.
- A non-XGIMI projector: no stock tree to import; write `menu/tree.json` by hand from the catalogue, add 1 to 2
  days.

## 6. How the Z9X stays provably unchanged

### 6.1 Stages 0 to 6: byte identity, nothing new to accept

The gate (`tools/play6/z9x_gate.sh:57-72`) reads `apps/Z9x*/`, `apps/common`, `apps/i18n`, `apps/sdk`,
`apps/LumenBridge`, `overlay/v1`, `overlay/apps_v1`, `overlay/debug`, `overlay/v65`, `tools/lumen`, `tools/sign`,
`tools/ota` and five single files. Everything this proposal adds lives in folders it does not read: `core/`,
`tools/gen/`, `tools/image/`, `devices/`, `installer/flows/`. So:

- The Z9X frozen lane builds 1.0.x exactly as today; `z9x_gate.sh` and `prove_unchanged.sh` keep proving it.
- `core/` is created once from the Z9X sources at a tagged commit ("fork once, on purpose"), then belongs to the
  new lane. Z9X files are read, never edited.
- Z9X data is extracted into `devices/horse_popular/` (not a gate input). An equivalence check proves the
  extracted tables match the frozen Java: every constant in `GmpfClient.java` / `Gmpf2Client.java` equals the
  `horse_popular` map row, every Z9X banned code in `apps/check_hal_callers.py:29` is BANNED in its
  `banned.tsv`. When `lumen gen horse_popular` exists, its `HalCodes.java` values are compared to the frozen
  constants on every check.

What the owner must accept in this window: **double maintenance**. A Z9X parity fix made in `apps/Z9xProjector`
must also be made in `core/` (or the reverse at the next Z9X release). `lumen check` prints a drift report
(core file vs its Z9X origin, informational, never red) so nothing is lost. The window should be short: stages 3
to 7 in about 3 to 5 weeks.

### 6.2 Stage 7: the Z9X switch release, behavioural proof

When the Z9X is built from `core/` plus `devices/horse_popular/`, its APK bytes change (generated classes,
different class layout). A byte pin cannot prove that. The owner must accept, for that one release, a proof made
of these parts instead:

1. HAL trace equality. Host tests run scripted user actions (open each menu page, change each value, keystone,
   focus, standby, wake) against the frozen Z9X app and against the new one, with a stubbed `android.os.HwBinder`
   on the test classpath that records (service, code, arguments). The frozen sources are not edited: the stub is
   test-only, the same technique as the hand-written stubs in `apps/HbProjector/test`. Both traces must be equal.
2. Menu equality on the owner's Z9X: uiautomator dump of every settings page with 1.0.x and with the new build,
   compared after removing ids. Same rows, same order, same values.
3. Host tests: the four Z9X tests (`FitTest`, `UiResTest`, `AkUnitsTest`, `DreamDefaultsTest`) green on the
   generated data.
4. OTA from the last 1.0.x to the switch build tested on the owner's Z9X, and the "Updater code -1" fix kept.
5. Owner OK, then `lumen record z9x --reason "switch to core"`. From then on the gate pins the new APKs and core
   becomes a Z9X input like `apps/common` is today, with pin rebuilds proving no change.

The alternative the owner can choose: never switch the Z9X. It stays on the frozen lane forever, fixes are made
twice forever, and the drift report is permanent. This is safe but gives up most of the speed gain for Z9X work.

## 7. How the checks change

| Today | Target |
|---|---|
| `z9x_gate.sh` protects folders, re-record by hand, 16 dated backups since 2026-10-12, 5 re-records on 2026-10-30 | same gate on the frozen lane until stage 7; one `lumen record z9x --reason` command; after stage 7 the gate proves outputs (pins) and treats `core/` like `apps/common` |
| `prove_unchanged.sh` compares counts in text ("16 of 16", 151 vs 152 callers) | per device bundle from the registry, compares exit codes and hash files; growth of a list is not a failure, a changed hash is |
| two fork checkers, 273 HB `same:` rows, 230 synced files, red on every Z9X round | no copies, so no fork rows; `lumen check` lists whole-file overrides with a count, warning in development, red only in a release build |
| three HAL checkers, fixed counts | one table-driven checker: dex transacts equal `map.tsv` rows; generator refuses banned codes |
| strings checked for Z9X only | every device, every locale, only strings the generated menu uses |
| tests: HB copies Z9X tests, Play 6 none | core tests run once per device with its generated data; plugin tests per device |
| image: compose plan compared for Play 6 only | compose plan and twice-build determinism for every device |
| publish audit by app name prefix | rules from the registry and `publish.rules` |
| no HB in combined runs | `lumen check all` |

New checks that exist only because of generation:
- generated files are up to date (regenerate into a temp dir, compare with `build/gen/X`),
- generators are deterministic (run twice, same bytes),
- no device identity checks in `core/` (grep for `isPlay6`, `Build.DEVICE`, codename strings),
- every menu node resolves (op mapped, feature ON, string present), else it is dropped and listed.

## 8. Staged migration plan

Each stage ends with a gate. A stage that does not pass its gate is not merged. "Z9X gate GREEN" means
`z9x_gate.sh` GREEN without re-record and `prove_unchanged.sh` passing.

| Stage | Work | Gate | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Green baseline | fix today's reds: Play 6 7 origin rows + `strings_fit.xml`, HB 4 origin rows, untracked `FitDevices.java`, stale count in `check_aidl_hal_test.sh`; refresh the baseline once with a reason | `check_forks --all` green, all HAL checks green, Z9X gate GREEN, `prove_unchanged.sh` PASS | 1 to 2 days |
| 1. Data extraction | write `devices/*/hal/map.tsv`, `features.tsv`, `behaviour.conf` for all three devices from current code; Z9X tables extracted from frozen Java | equivalence checks: extracted values equal current Java constants per device; Z9X gate GREEN (no gate input touched) | 2 to 3 days |
| 2. Generators and `lumen` CLI | `tools/gen/` halgen, featgen, behaviourgen, strgen; `lumen gen/check` | determinism (twice equal); for HB, generated `HalCodes` equals `AidlCaller` codes and `check_aidl_hal.py` passes on generated output; Z9X gate GREEN | 3 to 5 days |
| 3. Core + HB pilot | create `core/` from Z9X sources at a tag; HB builds from core + generated HAL, features, knobs; delete HB `same:` rows and `refresh_same.sh` | HB HAL trace equal to the previous HB build for the scripted suite; HB host tests green; HB test loop on the owner's G0130 (the `feedback-hb-test-loop` routine); Z9X gate GREEN | 1 to 1.5 weeks |
| 4. Menu engine | `core/menu` catalogue, `menu_import.py`, MenuEngine; HB menu from `menu/tree.json` imported from `dapengse` | uiautomator page dumps on HB equal to stage 3 build (or each difference listed and owner-approved as closer to stock); strings complete; Z9X gate GREEN | 1 week |
| 5. Play 6 onto core | Play 6 device-only code (`battery`, `speaker`, `lens`, `ambient`, `BootHandshake`, parts of `Play6PanelController`) into `devices/dragon_healthy/plugin`; renamed clients replaced by generated facades | Play 6 HAL trace equal to previous Play 6 build; Play 6 device test on the owner's unit; `check_play6_hal` semantics kept by the one checker; Z9X gate GREEN | 1.5 to 2 weeks |
| 6. Image, signer, installer | `compose.py` with steps; HB and Play 6 composed by it; one signer; ab-fastbootd flow; generated installer profiles | compose plan equal to before for Play 6 (`devices/_baseline/play6_compose/`) and HB; image built twice equal; installer goldens (43 Z9X cases, 99 Play 6 cases) unchanged; Z9X gate GREEN | 1.5 weeks |
| 7. Z9X switch release | Z9X from core + `devices/horse_popular`; retire frozen projector sources, `apps/common` sync, both fork tables | section 6.2 proof: HAL trace equality, menu dump equality on the owner's Z9X, host tests, OTA from 1.0.x, owner OK, one re-record with reason | 1 week plus the owner's release test |
| 8. Fourth device rehearsal | `lumen new-device` against a fixture device (fake dump with a stock tree from the 98) | from empty folder to a built APK and a compose plan in under one day of work; `lumen check all` green | 2 days |

Order rationale: the HB goes first because it is already 90 percent Z9X code with Z9X class names, so moving it
onto core is mostly deletion. The Play 6 goes second because it has the most real device code and gains the most
from plugins. The Z9X goes last, when the core has been proven on two devices.

## 9. Risks and limits

- Generators are code too. Keep them small, one per table, with golden tests in `tools/gen/test/`. If a
  generator grows past a few hundred lines, that part should probably be core Java instead.
- Codecs for structs (`KstPoint`, keystone arrays, EQ bands) stay hand-written in `core/hal/codec`; the table only
  names them. Not everything is generatable, and the proposal does not pretend it is.
- Stock trees describe stock menus, not Lumen menus. The importer gives a start and a to-do list; Lumen-only pages
  (voice, Lumen Play, AirPlay) are added to the tree by hand from the catalogue.
- Stock JSON and decompiled data stay private under `research/`; only the converted Lumen `tree.json` is device
  data, and `publish.rules` decides whether it is published.
- Double maintenance between stage 3 and stage 7 is real (section 6.1). If the Z9X switch slips, the drift grows.
- Performance: all resolution happens at build time; the APK holds static arrays. A runtime JSON menu would be
  slower on weak units and is ruled out.
